query: For additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components, what single intervention could improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the current fabrication baseline, defines the processing and application conditions under which it should hold, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying low‐amplitude ultrasonic vibration to the build platform during LPBF of CoCrFeMnNi high‐entropy alloy powder improves melt‐pool stability and grain refinement, resulting in enhanced dimensional precision, reduced porosity, and improved mechanical properties compared to standard LPBF without vibration.
generation.material_initial_state: Gas‐atomized CoCrFeMnNi HEA powder (15–45 µm) processed by conventional LPBF in argon.
generation.intervention: Continuous ultrasonic vibration (∼20 kHz, ≤5 µm amplitude) applied to the build platform during each laser‐melting layer.
generation.conditions: LPBF parameters: 200 W laser, 800 mm/s scan speed, 40 µm hatch, 20–50 µm layer thickness; argon atmosphere; room‐temperature water‐cooled build plate; ultrasonic vibration continuous at 20 kHz, ≤5 µm amplitude.
generation.structural_mediator: Acoustic streaming within the melt pool enhancing fluid flow, reducing gas entrapment and keyholing, and promoting uniform nucleation.
generation.mechanism: Ultrasonic waves induce pressure fluctuations in the melt pool that increase convection, break up spatter, and promote homogeneous solidification into finer equiaxed grains with lower residual stress and porosity, leading to tighter dimensions and higher strength.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved dimensional precision, reduced porosity, and modest gains in tensile strength and elongation relative to baseline; magnitudes uncertain.
generation.baseline: Conventional LPBF of CoCrFeMnNi HEA yields ~±100 µm dimensional deviation, ~1–2% porosity, ~800 MPa tensile strength, ~10% elongation.
generation.boundary: Valid for argon‐gas LPBF of CoCrFeMnNi HEA with layer thickness ≤50 µm and laser powers 150–250 W; untested for EBAM or other alloy systems.
generation.uncertainty: High, due to limited prior studies on ultrasonic‐assisted LPBF for HEAs.

falsification_experiment.design: Print two sets of tensile specimens under identical LPBF settings, one with ultrasonic vibration and one without. Use micro‐CT for porosity, 3D scanning for dimensional deviation, and tensile testing for mechanical properties.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If ultrasonic vibration yields no statistically significant (p<0.05) improvement in any of these metrics or shows change opposite to predicted direction, the hypothesis is falsified.
